headline: After 8 Months in Orbit, NASA Astronaut Chris Williams Returns Home
meta_description: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two cosmonauts safely landed after 241 days aboard the International Space Station, completing cancer research and critical m…
summary_short: After 241 days in space, NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts returned to Earth, having orbited the planet 3,856 times and traveled over 102 million…
body:
On July 26, NASA astronaut Chris Williams touched down safely in Kazakhstan after spending eight months aboard the International Space Station—a journey that saw him and his crewmates complete 3,856 orbits of Earth and travel more than 102 million miles. Williams, along with Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev, landed aboard the Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft near Dzhezkazgan at 5:27 a.m. CDT, marking the end of a mission launched on November 27, 2025. For both Williams and Mikaev, this was their first voyage to space; for Kud-Sverchkov, it was his second.

During his time in orbit, Williams contributed to research with tangible potential for humanity. His work included studies aimed at supporting the development of new cancer treatments, as well as investigations into producing advanced materials in space that could improve high-performance computers and electronics. Beyond laboratory work, he conducted two spacewalks—one to prepare the station's electrical power system for upgrades, and another to replace a faulty joint on the Canadarm2 robotic arm. These contributions represent more than routine maintenance; they directly advance both Earth-based medicine and NASA's long-term vision for lunar and Martian exploration.

The International Space Station has now supported continuous human presence for more than 25 years, and Williams's mission exemplifies why. The orbiting laboratory enables scientific breakthroughs impossible on Earth while providing essential knowledge about the demands of extended spaceflight. After landing in Kazakhstan, Williams will undergo medical evaluations before flying back to NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, ready to share what his eight months among the stars revealed.
quick_facts: NASA astronaut Chris Williams landed in Kazakhstan after 241 days in space
The crew orbited Earth 3,856 times and traveled over 102 million miles
Williams conducted two spacewalks, including work on the Canadarm2 robotic arm
His research included studies for new cancer treatment development
First space mission for Williams; second for cosmonaut Kud-Sverchkov
